name: Algeria
summary: The largest country in Africa by area, independent from France since 1962 after a long war of independence.

knownFor.label: Casbah of Algiers
knownFor.note: The old walled city, a World Heritage Site.

knownFor.label: Couscous
knownFor.note: Steamed semolina, shared across North Africa.

location.value: North Africa, from the Mediterranean deep into the Sahara; about 2.4 million km².

terrain.value: A fertile coastal strip, the Atlas Mountains and the Sahara.

climate.value: Mediterranean on the coast, desert inland.

resources.value: Oil and natural gas, farmland on the coast.

disasters.value: The Boumerdès earthquake of 2003 killed over 2,000 people; floods hit the Sahara and the coast.

urbanisation.value: Most Algerians live near the Mediterranean coast; Algiers is the capital and Oran the second city.

disease.value: Basic health care is free and good; the country was hit by COVID-19 in 2020–21.

migration.value: About a million European settlers left in 1962; Algerians emigrated to France.

tradeRoutes.value: Natural gas pipelines run under the Mediterranean to Spain and Italy.

wealth.value: An upper-middle-income country, with oil and gas as the main source of wealth.

inequality.value: Youth unemployment is high, and wealth is concentrated among the elite.

governmentType.value: A semi-presidential republic, with a strong role for the army.

keyRulers.value: Ahmed Ben Bella (first president from 1962, overthrown by Houari Boumédiène in 1965); Abdelaziz Bouteflika (1999–2 April 2019, resigned after mass protests). Later and present leaders are not named here.

succession.value: Elections, often disputed; one party ruled until 1989.

institutions.value: A strong presidency, an influential army and a parliament.

stability.value: Civil war in the 1990s (more than 100,000 deaths, figures disputed); Hirak protests (2019).

eliteConflict.value: Power struggles within the army and ruling elite.

armyAndTech.value: One of the largest armies in Africa, which has long had a major role in politics.

majorWars.value: War of Independence (1954–62); the 1990s civil war.

territoryChange.value: The borders have remained the same since independence in 1962.

alliancesRivals.value: Non-aligned; ties with Russia; rivalry with Morocco.

inventions.value: No major inventions in modern times; Algeria is known for its Roman ruins and Casbah of Algiers.

scienceEducation.value: Free schooling and universities, with literacy rising since independence.

openness.value: Mixed, with strong state control over the economy and the media.

communicationTransport.value: Railways and roads along the coast; the East–West Highway.

religion.value: Sunni Islam is the official religion, practised by about 99% (98.2% in the infobox for 2025).

languageWriting.value: Arabic and Tamazight (official since 2016); French widely used.

artsArchitecture.value: Writers such as Kateb Yacine and Assia Djebar; raï music.

socialStructure.value: Arab and Amazigh (Berber) communities, with a large young population.

sharedIdentity.value: Identity shaped by the independence struggle.

dailyLife.value: City apartments and village houses; couscous, bread, mint tea.

neighbours.value: Morocco, Tunisia, Libya, Niger, Mali, Mauritania.

colonisation.value: A French colony from 1830 to 1962 (formally annexed in 1848).

riseSignals.value: Independence after the war, confirmed by referendum in 1962.

peakPeriod.value: The page gives no peak. Hydrocarbons are about 60% of budget revenue, 30% of GDP and 87.7% of export earnings.

declineSignals.value: Falling oil prices in the 1980s and unrest that led to the civil war of the 1990s.

outcome.value: Algeria continues as an independent republic.

overallCertainty.value: Well documented; civil war casualty figures disputed.
